title: A reliable channel over unreliable packets
hints: Keep three separate pieces of state: what you are sending (the queue, and which message ids went into each sequence number), what you have received (the ack and its bits), and what you are delivering (the next id and a buffer of early arrivals). Each part of `receive` touches only one of them.

Give queued messages a 32-bit internal id that never wraps, and write only its low 16 bits into packets. Matching an acknowledged packet back to its messages is then never ambiguous on the sending side.
Validate the whole packet into a temporary list before changing anything. Then "a malformed packet changes nothing" is automatic.
requirements: Every packet has the exact layout above and is at most 1 200 bytes.
Acks are piggybacked on every packet and each sent packet is acknowledged at most once.
Reliable messages are resent only when due, and leave the queue when acknowledged.
Messages are delivered exactly once and in order, despite loss, delay, reordering and duplicates.
Message ids and sequence numbers keep working after they wrap.
stretch: Replace the fixed `resendAfter` with the `RttEstimator` of practice 5.04, sampling the time from sending each packet to its first ack, and add an unreliable channel whose messages go in the next packet only and are never resent.
